items.title: Section: Malice's Five Aspects, Paralleling Covetousness

items.zh: 何等名為瞋恚五相？一、有增惡心，謂於能損害相隨法分別故。二、有不堪耐心。謂於不饒益不堪忍故。三、有怨恨心，謂於不饒益數不如理隨憶念故。四、有謀略心，謂於有情作如是意：何當捶撻、何當殺害，乃至廣說故。五、有覆蔽心，謂如前說。
items.en: What are the five aspects of malice? First, a mind of hatred, arising through discrimination following the mark of what causes harm. Second, a mind of intolerance, unable to bear what is disadvantageous. Third, a mind of resentment, repeatedly and unreasonably dwelling on what is disadvantageous. Fourth, a mind of scheming, thinking towards a being: how might I strike them, how might I kill them, and so on at length. Fifth, a mind of obscuration, as already explained.

items.title: Section: Wrong View's Five Aspects — Closing Self-Nature, Opening Method

items.zh: 於此五相隨闕一種，即非圓滿瞋恚之相；若具一切，方名圓滿。何等名為邪見五相？一、有愚癡心，謂不如實了所知故。二、有暴酷心，謂樂作諸惡故。三、有越流行心，謂於諸法不如理分別推求故。四、有失壞心，謂無施與、愛養、祠祀等，誹謗一切妙行等故。五、有覆蔽心，謂邪見纏之所覆蔽，不覺羞恥，不知過患及出離故。於此五相隨闕一種，即非圓滿邪見之相；具一切分，乃名圓滿。復次，若以手等害諸眾生，說名殺生。如是以塊、杖刀、縛錄、斷食、折挫、治罰、呪藥、厭禱、尸半尸等害諸眾生，皆名殺生。
items.en: Should any one of these five aspects be missing, it is not the complete mark of malice; only possessing all of them is it called complete. What are the five aspects of wrong view? First, a mind of delusion, failing to truly understand what is known. Second, a mind of cruelty, delighting in every evil deed. Third, a mind transgressing the stream, arising from unreasoned speculation about the dharmas. Fourth, a mind of destruction, denying giving, loving care, reverent offering, and slandering every excellent conduct. Fifth, a mind of obscuration, covered by the entangling grip of wrong view, feeling no shame, recognising neither its fault nor the need to escape it. Should any one of these five be missing, it is not the complete mark of wrong view; possessing every part, it is called complete. Moreover, killing living beings with the hand and the like is called killing. Likewise killing living beings with a clod, a staff, a blade, by binding and confining, by cutting off food, by tormenting, by punishing, by spells and potions, by curses and imprecations, and by corpse or half-corpse, are all called killing.

items.title: Section: For Profit, For Fear, For Sport — The Motives Behind Wrongdoing

items.zh: 為財利等害諸眾生，亦名殺生。或怨為損、或為除怨、或謂為法，乃至或為戲樂害諸眾生，亦名殺生。若自殺害，若令他害，皆得殺罪。復次，若有顯然劫他財物，名不與取。如是竊盜、攻牆解結、伏道竊奪，或有拒債、受寄不還。或行誑諂矯詐而取，或現怖畏方便而取，或現威德而取彼物，或自劫盜，或復令他，如是一切皆不與取。或有自為，或有為他，或怖畏故，或為殺縛，或為折伏，或為受用，或為給侍，或憎嫉故不與而取，此等皆名不與取罪。
items.en: Killing living beings for the sake of wealth and profit is also called killing. Also, out of fear of being harmed, or to eliminate an enemy, or believing it to be lawful, and so on, even killing living beings for sport is also called killing. Whether one kills personally or causes another to kill, the offence of killing is incurred either way. Moreover, openly robbing another of their wealth is called taking what is not given. Likewise stealth theft, breaking through walls and undoing bonds, ambush along the road, refusing a debt, failing to return what was entrusted, taking through deception and fraud, taking through a display of fear, or taking through a display of authority, whether stealing oneself or causing another to steal, all of this is taking what is not given. Whether for oneself, for another, out of fear, to avoid being killed or bound, to subdue another, for one's own use, to provide for dependents, or out of envy, taking what has not been given — all of these are called the offence of taking what is not given.

items.zh: 復次，若行不應行，名欲邪行。或於非支、非時、非處、非量、非理，如是一切皆欲邪行。

items.title: Section: Wrong Part, Wrong Time, Wrong Place — Sexual Misconduct Catalogued

items.zh: 若於母等、母等所護，如經廣說，名不應行。一切男及不男，屬自屬他，皆不應行。除產門外，所有餘分皆名非支。若穢下時、胎圓滿時、飲兒乳時、受齋戒時，或有病時，謂所有病匪宜習欲，是名非時。若諸尊重所集會處，或靈廟中，或大眾前，或堅鞕地高下不平，令不安隱，如是等處說名非處。過量而行，名為非量。是中量者，極至於五。此外一切皆名過量。不依世禮，故名非理。若自行欲，若媒合他，此二皆名欲邪行攝。若有公顯，或復隱竊，或因誑諂方便矯亂，或因委託而行邪行，如是皆名欲邪行罪。
items.en: Approaching one's mother or a woman protected by another, as explained at length in the sutras, is not to be done. Any man and anyone not fully male, whether belonging to oneself or another, is not to be approached. Apart from the birth passage, every other part is called the wrong part. During menstruation, at the completion of pregnancy, while nursing a child, while observing the precepts, or during illness unsuited to such activity, is called the wrong time. Any hall where the venerable gather, any shrine, before a crowd, or on hard and uneven ground causing discomfort, is called the wrong place. Exceeding the proper measure is called excess; the measure here is five at most, and anything beyond is excess. Not following worldly custom is called impropriety. Whether engaging personally or arranging it for another, both belong to sexual misconduct. Whether done openly or in secret, through deception, or by abusing entrusted intimacy, all of this is the offence of sexual misconduct.

items.title: Section: How a Lie Travels, and the Many Faces of a Cutting Word

items.zh: 復次，若自因故而說妄語，或他因故，或因怖畏，或因財利而說妄語，皆名妄語。若不見聞覺知言見聞覺知，或見聞覺知言不見聞覺知，皆名妄語。若書陳說，或以默然表忍斯義，或動支體以表其相，或為證說，或有自說，或令他說，如是一切皆妄語罪。復次，若以實事毀呰於他，為乖離故而發此言，名離間語。或以不實假合方便以為依止，為損壞他而有陳說，或依親近施與、或依知友給侍而有陳說，名離間語。若自利緣，或損他緣，或由他教，或現破德，或現怖畏，為乖離故，或自發言、或令他發，如是皆名離間語罪。復次，若有對面發辛楚言，名麁惡語。或不現前，或對大眾，或幽僻處，或隨實過不隨實過，或書表示，或假現相，或依自說，或依他說，或因掉舉，或因不靜，或依種族過失，或依依止過失，或依作業禁戒現行過失，或自發起辛楚之言，或令他發，如是皆名麁惡語罪。
items.en: Moreover, speaking falsely for one's own sake, for another's sake, out of fear, or for material gain, is all called false speech. Saying one has seen, heard, sensed, or known what one has not, or saying one has not when one has, is all called false speech. Moreover, using a true matter to disparage another, speaking so as to cause estrangement, is called divisive speech. Or relying on a fabricated, unreal matter, speaking so as to harm another. Moreover, delivering cutting words to another's face is called harsh speech. Whether not in their presence, before a crowd, or in a secluded place, whether following a genuine or invented fault, in writing, or through a feigned manner, whether spoken by oneself or by another, whether from agitation or from lack of calm, whether grounded in a fault of lineage, a fault of bodily basis, or a fault of conduct and precepts, whether arising from oneself or induced in another, all of this is the offence of harsh speech.

items.zh: 復次，若有依舞而發歌詞，名為綺語。或依作樂，或復俱依，或俱不依而發歌詞，皆名綺語。若佛法外能引無義所有書論，以愛樂心受持讚美，以大音聲而為諷頌，廣為他人開示分別，皆名綺語。若依鬪訟諍競發言，或樂處眾宣說王論、臣論、賊論，廣說乃至國土等論，皆名綺語。若說妄語、或離間語、或麁惡語，下至不思不擇發無義言，皆名綺語。

blocks.text: The last mental courses, then the motives and methods behind each wrong act.
Master Cháng Bǎi: with intolerance of the other's harm, malice arises; resentment dwells repeatedly on it. One thinks how to strike or ruin the other, and feels no shame.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one thinks there is no giving, that giving brings no good result; no loving care, that caring for parents and teachers brings none. It goes against the flow of the wholesome.

Master Cháng Bǎi: killing personally or inciting another both bring the offence. Not repaying debts or returning what was entrusted is taking what is not given. Falsely displaying meditation or a dignified manner to obtain offerings is also theft.
Master Cháng Bǎi: arranging misconduct for others is also misconduct. The treatise lists wrong times, places, and measures; its concern includes others' health and the sanctity of shrines.

Master Cháng Bǎi: claiming to have seen what one has not, or denying what one has, is lying. Using a true matter to split people is still divisive speech. (Untranslated, 0631c15: idle chatter includes songs, absorbing worldly books, gossip about kings and thieves, and any thoughtless meaningless speech.)
"Using a true matter to split people is still divisive speech." Truthfulness alone is not enough; the intention matters.

quiz.q: What are the five aspects of malice?
options: attachment, greed, gluttony, scheming, obscuration, the same five as covetousness
quiz.why: The treatise lists these. Master Cháng Bǎi: with intolerance towards the other's harm, malice arises; resentment dwells repeatedly on what is against the other. Notice that scheming and obscuration recur across all three mental paths. The English "hatred" here and "malice" elsewhere render one word.

quiz.q: How are malice's scheming and obscured minds explained?
options: thinking how to strike or kill; no shame, not knowing anger's fault
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one thinks how to strike or kill the other, or bring them all manner of misery; having given rise to anger one feels no shame, not knowing that revenge is wrong or anger harmful. The source's closing sentence on completeness is at §39 in the English.

quiz.q: When are the five aspects of malice and wrong view complete?
options: lacking any one, not complete; only with all
three suffice, the first three being chief, 隨闕 referring only to those
quiz.why: The rule is the same for all three mental paths. Master Cháng Bǎi's account of wrong view's aspects includes a cruel mind delighting in evil and being so veiled as to feel no shame and not seek to leave wrong thinking. The English "complete mark" for 圓滿 is fine.

quiz.q: The English has "a mind transgressing the stream." What is the problem?
options: it omits 善: what is crossed is the wholesome stream; "stream" may suggest stream-entry
no problem: it means crossing saṃsāra's stream, the holder imagining this
it should be "going with the flow"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this unwholesome mind goes beyond the wholesome stream, through improper discrimination about the Three Jewels and four truths; it goes against the flow of wholesome activity. Without "wholesome," the English stream could be taken for saṃsāra or the stream-enterer's stream.

quiz.q: What is wrong view's mind of destruction?
options: a mood from losing health, the sick being discouraged, unrelated to denying giving, the lecture's examples being patients
slandering giving, care, and offering, denying good results
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one thinks there is no giving, that giving brings no good result; no loving care, that respecting and caring for parents or teachers brings none. So what is destroyed is the root of good. The English "a mind of destruction" is literal but acceptable.

quiz.q: What of killing personally or by another, and killing thought lawful?
options: only one's own hand; thinking it lawful removes guilt
both incur the offence; killing thinking it lawful is still killing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: killing personally or inciting another both bring the offence of killing; thinking human sacrifice lawful, or that worship requires killing fowl, is killing through wrong view. The English "believing it to be lawful" is correct for 謂為法.

quiz.q: The English has "refusing to give and taking anyway." What is wrong with the subject?
options: no problem: not giving and also taking shows greed, as the treatise and lecture say
it is taking what the owner has not given; the English has the taker refusing to give
quiz.why: 不與取 means taking what the owner has not given. Master Cháng Bǎi's examples are refusing to repay debts and not returning what was entrusted, which are ways of keeping what is not one's own. The English "refusing to give" shifts refusal to the taker, and contradicts the path's own definition at §34.

quiz.q: Which methods count as theft, and does deception?
options: only open robbery, stealth and debts being civil matters
robbery, stealth, refusing debts, keeping deposits, and deceit all count
quiz.why: The treatise's list is broad. Master Cháng Bǎi's example: falsely displaying absorption or the noble path, and a dignified manner, to obtain others' offerings. So religious pretence is a form of theft. The English is generally accurate.

quiz.q: The English has "engaging personally or arranging through another." What is wrong with the direction?
options: no problem: it is using a go-between for oneself, the go-between being blameless, as the lecture says
媒合他 is matching others; the English reads as arranging for oneself through someone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if one engages in misconduct oneself, or acts as go-between for others to complete it, both are sexual misconduct. So the one who arranges is also guilty. The English "through another" reverses this. The same section's "improper reasoning" for 非理 is also off.

quiz.q: What are the wrong time and the wrong place?
options: daytime is wrong and night proper; outside the home is wrong, by custom
menstruation, late pregnancy, nursing, precept days; assemblies of the venerable, shrines
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi lists these times for a woman and the observance days, and explains the place as halls where the respected gather and temples. The list shows care for health and reverence. The English "the proper place" for 產門 can be confused with 非處 in the same section.

quiz.q: What is the measure in "exceeding the proper measure"?
options: ten at most, by the ten wholesome paths, counted over a lifetime rather than one occasion
five at most; anything beyond is excess
quiz.why: The treatise sets a measure of five. Master Cháng Bǎi sums up the prior item: a woman under another's protection is not to be approached. The English "Exceeding the proper measure" is clear. The treatise then defines 非理 as not following worldly propriety, which the English mistranslates.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain false speech's forms and the eel-wrigglers?
options: only lies for gain count, those of fear not; eel-wrigglers are advanced
claiming what one lacks or the reverse, hiding one's thought; eel-wrigglers lie fearing exposure of ignorance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: claiming to have seen or heard what one has not, or denying what one has, concealing what one thinks; eel-wrigglers lie out of fear that others will learn of their ignorance. The English "for material gain" fits the motives. "Seen, heard, sensed, known" is standard.

quiz.q: Is truthful speech that divides still divisive, and how far does harsh speech extend?
options: no: truth is never faulty; harsh speech is only to the face, absent targets being unhurt
yes: spoken to split, it counts; harsh speech extends beyond the face, to writing or inciting
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though the matter is true, using it to split people is divisive speech; harsh words raised by oneself or by inciting others are all the offence. So truth does not by itself excuse speech. The source's closing clause on divisive speech is lost in the English.
